hero.body: is a Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) system that turns your strategy into professional algorithmic trading. Manage 14 AI-based and deterministic agents. Let them watch the market 24/7 and act within your guardrails.
hero.rot2: On your desktop, server or cloud.

transparency.body: is software, not a service. Write your own prompt for a local model or Google Gemini; its answer is only a shortlist. 14 quant agents, each a piece of software with one discipline, rate every pick against the weights and thresholds you set. The deterministic Iron Dome applies your risk limits last. The AI never places an order. You start on a paper account, and the decisions and the risk stay with you. No investment advice.

profit.intro: You design the strategy. Set the rules for the agents and the Iron Dome: stock selection, risk management, limits. autonomous_ executes.

p1.text: Number of positions, order size, entry thresholds, stops, exposure, trades per day. And you weight the 14 agents.

p2.text: Order size, exposure and your own limits are checked before anything is sent. It enforces your limits; it cannot prevent losses.

p3.text: Stop all trading at any time with one click, and sell all positions if you choose.

p4.text: Every installation starts with play money and live market data. Real money only moves after your explicit approval.

audit.intro: Read the code, check every decision, extend it with your own logic. autonomous_ is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence.

p1.text: Each agent states its argument in plain text. You see who voted, how strongly and why.

p2.text: Decisions are written to a hash-chained log. Any later change to an entry becomes visible.

p3.text: The core is published under the Apache 2.0 licence. Read what it does, line by line.

p4.text: Compare decisions with outcomes, adjust a rule, run it again in paper mode. Your strategy improves on evidence, not on memory.

safe.intro: Your broker keys, your strategy and your trading history stay on your own computer or server, not with us. autonomous_ keeps your data with you.

p1.text: Broker API keys are stored encrypted in your operating system's keychain.

p2.text: On the desktop, the AI model runs locally by default. No dependence on a cloud AI provider.

p3.text: No usage data leaves your computer unless you switch it on.

p4.text: The software has no function for withdrawals or transfers. Your money stays at your broker.

agents.lede: 14 agents look at the market from different angles, AI-based and deterministic. Each casts a weighted vote with a written reason. The AI has no direct line to your broker: its votes feed into deterministic rules, and those rules decide whether and how much to trade, inside your limits. You choose which agents vote and how much each vote counts.

quant.intro: Your AI suggests stocks. 14 quant agents, AI-based and deterministic software, rate every suggestion against the rules you set: which agents vote, how much each vote counts and which thresholds a pick has to pass. They apply your rules. They do not manage your money.

p1.text: Fundamentals from SEC EDGAR filings, valuation, quality, momentum, trend, volume, market regime, VIX, news sentiment, drawdown. Each agent looks at one thing and states what it finds.

p2.text: You decide how much each agent counts and whether it votes at all.

p3.text: A pick passes only if it meets the limits you set: consensus, valuation, volatility, position size.

p4.text: Your prompt decides which stocks reach the table. Whether one is bought follows from your rules, applied by the agents and the Iron Dome, never from the language model.

trail.intro: No black box. For every run you see which model answered, which version of your prompt it used, how each quant agent rated each pick and why it passed or failed.

p1.text: Each agent states its argument in plain text. You see who voted, how strongly and why.

p2.text: Time, prompt version, model and provider, suggested and dropped tickers.

p3.text: Every edit of your prompt or your rules is written to the hash-chained log before it applies.

p4.text: Run your prompt against the bundled SEC EDGAR snapshot. Past periods are flagged, because a language model already knows that history.
